turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same n-i-p (regular) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
Using the training set, I looked for candidates that sit in the same device “motifs” as the highest-efficiency reproducible recipes, then filtered them by device-physics considerations:

- **Electron-selective contact / band alignment:** the strongest training motifs contain **SnO₂**, **PCBM/C₆₀ fullerene interlayers**, or **TiO₂/SnO₂ cascades**. These give good electron extraction and suppress hole leakage.
- **Hole-selective contact:** **PTAA**, **Spiro-MeOTAD**, and the high-work-function organic stack in the TaTm/F6-TCNNQ family are repeatedly associated with higher efficiencies, especially when paired with a high-work-function anode.
- **Interface recombination / passivation:** PCBM/C₆₀ interlayers, HMDS passivation, and oxide passivation layers tend to raise voltage and reproducibility.
- **Back-contact chemistry:** **Au** and **MoOₓ/Au** are generally safer and more selective than bare Ag, although Ag can work well when separated by fullerene/organic HTL stacks.
- **Deposition quality:** spin-coating-based recipes with known high-efficiency analogs are preferred over unusual or poorly matched deposition routes; co-evaporation is credible when the training analog is strong.

### Most promising candidates

1. **c005** — `SLG | ITO / TiO2-c | PCBM-60 / PCDTBT8 / MoO3 | Au / Spin >> Spin`  
   Very close to the training recipe `FTO / TiO2-c | PCBM-60 / PCDTBT1 / MoO3 | Au / Spin >> Spin` at **19.35%**. PCBM passivates the electron-contact interface, PCDTBT-type HTL is credible, and MoO₃/Au is an excellent stable anode.

2. **c068** — `SLG | ITO / SnO2-np | TiO2-np / PTAA / Au | MoO3 / Spin`  
   Matches the high-efficiency SnO₂/PTAA region of the training data, e.g. `ITO / SnO2-np / PTAA / Ag / Spin` at **18.19%**, and PTAA/Au-type anodes also appear in other high rows. SnO₂ gives strong electron selectivity; PTAA gives good hole extraction; MoO₃/Au reduces contact recombination.

3. **c017** — `SLG | ITO / C60; PhIm | C60 / TaTM | F6-TCNNQ; TaTm / Ag / Co-evaporation`  
   Almost identical to the training stack `ITO / C60; Phlm | C60 / TaTm | F6-TCNNQ; TaTm / Au / Co-evaporation` at **17.9%**. The fullerene ETL plus doped small-molecule HTL is highly selective, and co-evaporation can give dense, reproducible films.

4. **c064** — `SLG | FTO / TiO2-c | SnO2-np / Spiro-MeOTAD / Au / Spin`  
   Belongs to the same family as the very high `FTO / TiO2-c | SnO2-np / Spiro-MeOTAD / Ag / Spin >> Dipp` recipe at **20.85%**, and also related to `TiO2-c | SnO2 / Spiro / Ag` at **17.47%**. It is slightly penalized relative to those because it lacks the extra passivation/dipping step and uses a simpler spin-only process, but the TiO₂/SnO₂/Spiro/Au stack is still physically strong.

5. **c073** — `SLG | ITO-HMDS Scaffold / TiO2-c | C60 / PTAA / Ag / Spin`  
   Close to `ITO / TiO2-c | C60 / PTAA / Ag / Spin` at **16.5%**, with the added benefit of an HMDS passivated scaffold. C₆₀ improves electron selectivity and passivation, PTAA is a strong HTL, and the HMDS layer should reduce interfacial recombination/shunting.

Near misses such as **c080**, **c045**, **c021**, and several custom-HTL TiO₂-mp devices are plausible, but they either rely on less-proven interfaces, more problematic back-contact chemistry, flexible substrates, or nanostructures likely to add recombination.

Final: c005, c068, c017, c064, c073
